title: Create the GitHub repository, protect main, add the team, load labels and issue templates
acceptance: Repository tahseel-ai exists; main requires a pull request and a passing check; all five members are collaborators; labels loaded with .github/labels.sh.
ai_tip: Ask the AI to explain each branch-protection setting before you tick it.

title: Create the repository skeleton: folders, .gitignore, .env.example, pre-commit hooks
acceptance: backend/, frontend/, data/, evals/, deploy/ exist with a README each; .env is ignored; .env.example lists every variable without values; pre-commit runs formatting and a secret scan.
ai_tip: Good first task for the AI: generate a .gitignore for Python plus Node, then review every line.

title: Docker Compose basics: database with pgvector, backend, frontend, health check
acceptance: docker compose up starts the database, the backend, and the frontend on a clean machine; /health returns OK; pgvector extension is enabled.
ai_tip: AI knows Compose syntax well; verify image versions and that the pgvector image is the one you intend.

title: Continuous integration: lint and tests on every pull request
acceptance: A GitHub Actions workflow runs lint and the test suite for backend and frontend; a failing check blocks merging.
ai_tip: Have the AI write the workflow, then break a test on purpose to prove the check fails.

title: Data model and migrations for the 19 tables
acceptance: SQLAlchemy models and Alembic migrations create all 19 tables with the keys, enumerations, and indexes in the Database Design part; tenant_id on every table except tenants.
ai_tip: The ERD and dictionary are generated from the PRD: give the AI the dictionary and check every field name against it.

title: Authentication, users, and the three roles
refs: FR-35; AC-014; Decision Log D15, D30
acceptance: Users sign in; roles Owner, Finance Manager, Collector are enforced on the server; a Collector sees only assigned customers; only the Owner manages users.
ai_tip: Treat AI output for auth as untrusted: have a second person review it, and test the forbidden paths, not only the happy ones.

title: Tenant-scoped data layer and the cross-tenant test
acceptance: All reads and writes go through one tenant-scoped layer; a test proves tenant A cannot read tenant B, including through a vector query.
ai_tip: Ask the AI to try to break your layer: have it list ways a query could skip the tenant filter.

title: Receivables engine: outstanding, overdue, aging, KPIs, with unit tests
refs: FR-04; FR-05; AC-002; PRD sections 10 and 15
acceptance: Computes outstanding, days overdue, aging buckets, average days beyond terms, and DSO. Overdue is never stored; payments are the source of truth; tests cover partial payments and edge dates.
ai_tip: Write the tests from the PRD formulas first, then let the AI propose the code. Never accept a formula you did not check against the PRD.

title: Risk score engine: factors, caps, rounding, tenant settings
acceptance: Score 0 to 100 from the four factors with default weights 30/25/25/20; factor points are rounded and add up to the score; weights are read from tenant_settings; tests prove the arithmetic.
ai_tip: Ask the AI to write property-style tests (points never exceed weights, sum equals score). Check the worked ABC example (70).

title: Priority, urgency, and the suggested-action rules
acceptance: Priority = risk x overdue exposure x urgency, scaled so the top account is 100; urgency from the default events; suggested action follows the six rules in order; disputed invoices are excluded.
ai_tip: Give the AI the rule order verbatim and ask for one test per rule.

title: Tenant settings and policy rules services with seeded defaults
refs: FR-12; FR-13; AC-011; Decision Log D21, D22
acceptance: tenant_settings validated by a typed schema; policy_rules with source document and section; changes are audited; defaults load from the seed script.
ai_tip: AI is good at typed schemas; verify the defaults against the PRD section 11 and 12.

title: Cash forecast with range and confidence, plus the backtest harness
acceptance: Expected cash for 7 and 30 days with low, expected, and high values and a confidence label; never worded as guaranteed; a time-split backtest runs on synthetic data.
ai_tip: Ask the AI to explain the method back to you before it writes code; if you cannot explain it, do not merge it.

title: Synthetic data generator with realistic patterns
acceptance: About 120 customers and 1,500 invoices over 12 months with reliable, late, and chronic payers, partial payments, broken promises, disputes, strategic accounts, and noise. A fixed seed gives the same data.
ai_tip: The AI can draft the generator; you decide the patterns. Check the output distributions with a quick chart.

title: Seed script: tenants, users, settings, rules, sample policies
acceptance: One command loads a demo tenant with users in all three roles, default settings, rules, and the sample policy documents.
ai_tip: Keep passwords for demo users in .env.example, never in the code.

title: Sample policy documents (about 20), including conflicting and missing cases
acceptance: About 20 short policy and template documents in English and Arabic, some with deliberately conflicting sections, and a list of questions that have no matching policy.
ai_tip: Use the AI for first drafts, then have a native speaker review the Arabic. Mark all of it as synthetic.

title: Import API: parse CSV and Excel, mapping, validation, preview
acceptance: Upload, mapping, validation (duplicates, missing due dates), and a preview that imports nothing until confirmed; partial payments handled.
ai_tip: Test with deliberately messy files; ask the AI to generate ugly sample files.

title: LLM-assisted column mapping from headers and masked sample rows
acceptance: The model proposes a mapping from the headers and a few masked rows; the user confirms; no unmasked personal data is sent.
ai_tip: Check the prompt that is actually sent, not the one you intended to send.

title: Receivables Health Report endpoint
acceptance: After the first upload the endpoint returns aging, risk distribution, the top 20 accounts to chase, and expected cash.
ai_tip: Reuse the engine functions; the AI should not re-implement calculations.

title: LLMClient: OpenRouter, timeouts, retries, fallback, cost logging
refs: Decision Log D12; FR-21; Technical_Strength ADR-9
acceptance: One interface for all model calls; model IDs per task in config; timeouts, retries, and a fallback model; tokens, cost, and latency written to agent_runs.
ai_tip: Never paste a real API key into an AI chat. Use a throwaway key with a spending limit.

title: Policy ingestion: parse, chunk, embed, store with the tenant filter
refs: FR-10; PRD section 14; Decision Log D16
acceptance: Documents are parsed, chunked with metadata, embedded with a multilingual model, and stored in pgvector; every search filters by tenant inside the query.
ai_tip: Test with Arabic and mixed queries before choosing the embedding model.

title: retrieve_policy tool: rules, passages, citations, honest refusal
refs: FR-11; FR-12; AC-004; Decision Log D21
acceptance: Returns triggered rules and cited passages; says no relevant policy was found; flags conflicting passages for human review.
ai_tip: Include documents with instructions inside them to test injection (task T-072).

title: Agent orchestrator: tool-calling loop, tool registry, logging, number post-check
refs: FR-19; FR-20; FR-22; Decision Log D13
acceptance: A plain loop that calls tools, logs every call, never calculates, and checks that every number in the answer appears in a tool result.
ai_tip: Read every line of the loop yourself; it is the heart of the system.

title: Agent tools: receivables, risk, priority, history, KPIs, forecast
acceptance: Each tool wraps an engine function with a typed schema and tenant scoping; no tool writes customer memory.
ai_tip: Ask the AI for the tool schemas; check that the schemas match the function signatures.

title: Customer memory API: notes, call results, promises, promise status rule
refs: FR-14; FR-15; FR-18; AC-009; Decision Log D28
acceptance: Humans record notes, call results, and promises with author, time, and source; promise status is derived by rule; managers can soft-delete an entry, which is audited.
ai_tip: The AI must not be given any way to write to this API; confirm that in review.

title: Note embeddings and the recall tool
acceptance: Notes are embedded on save; the agent can answer what was agreed last time and cites the note; the interface can list the memories used.
ai_tip: Test retrieval quality with a handful of realistic Arabic and English notes.

title: Conversation memory: threads, last N turns, labeled summary
acceptance: Threads store messages; the last N turns are injected; a summary is stored with is_summary and labeled AI-generated; nothing moves into customer memory automatically.
ai_tip: Write a test that a summary never becomes a customer note.

title: Draft generator: Arabic, tones, tier defaults, rule-based draft check
acceptance: Drafts in formal, friendly, and firm tones; the default follows the tier; a rule-based check flags legal threats and forbidden phrases; numbers in a draft come from tools.
ai_tip: The AI can write drafts; a native speaker must review the Arabic. Keep a list of phrases the check must catch.

title: Recommendations and the approval gate
refs: FR-25; FR-26; AC-005; AC-014; Technical_Strength ADR-4
acceptance: Recommendations start pending; approve, edit, and reject store original and edited text with a reason; the API rejects executing an unapproved recommendation; flagged items need a manager.
ai_tip: Write the failing test first: try to execute an unapproved recommendation and expect a rejection.

title: Tasks and the append-only audit log
acceptance: Tasks are created only from approved recommendations; every recommendation, approval, edit, rejection, and tool call is written to audit_logs; the application role cannot update or delete it.
ai_tip: Have the AI draft the database grants, then test them with the real application user.

title: Guardrails: dispute status and the reminder cap
refs: FR-28; FR-29; AC-012; AC-013; Decision Log D23
acceptance: A person sets and a manager clears disputed; disputed invoices leave the ranking and alert the manager; beyond the cap a draft needs an override.
ai_tip: List the edge cases with the AI (partly disputed customers, cap at the boundary) and write a test for each.

title: Relationship-aware recommendation for strategic accounts
acceptance: A strategic customer gets the suggested action to talk to the sales rep first, before any contact.
ai_tip: Small and clear: a good first task for the AI to implement and a person to verify.

title: Frontend skeleton: Next.js, TypeScript, EN/AR dictionaries, RTL, navigation by role
acceptance: Both languages from the first page; no hard-coded strings; CSS logical properties; Western digits and Intl formats; navigation shows what each role may see.
ai_tip: Ask the AI to review your CSS for physical properties (left, right) that should be logical.

title: Import screen
acceptance: Four steps (upload, map, validate, preview) matching the wireframe, in both languages.
ai_tip: Give the AI the wireframe image and the HTML source from docs/diagrams/wireframes.

title: Executive dashboard
acceptance: Cards, expected cash with range and confidence, aging, and top accounts, matching the wireframe in both languages.
ai_tip: Use the generated sample data, not typed-in numbers.

title: Collection Queue screen
acceptance: Ranked list with risk badge, priority, suggested action, manager-review tag, and the disputed list link.
ai_tip: Make sure the risk level shows a word and a number, not only a color.

title: Customer Profile screen with the note, call result, and promise form
acceptance: Summary cards, factor bars, invoices, notes and promises, and the form that records memory with author and time.
ai_tip: Check keyboard access and the Arabic layout on this screen specifically.

title: AI recommendation panel with all states
acceptance: Recommendation, reasons, rule and passage, memory used, draft with tone, approve/edit/reject, and the four honest states.
ai_tip: Test each state with real API responses, not mocks only.

title: Settings, policy rules, and documents screens
acceptance: Managers can edit tenant settings, confirm policy rules, and upload documents.
ai_tip: Cut this first if time is short (Decision Log, section E).

title: Review all Arabic interface text
acceptance: A native speaker reviews every Arabic string for meaning and tone and fixes the dictionary.
ai_tip: Use the AI to find inconsistent terms, but the final judgment is the native speaker's.

title: Evaluation harness and the basic eval sets
refs: FR-36; Technical_Strength section 5; Decision Log D29
acceptance: About 15 agent cases, 10 retrieval queries, and 5 safety tests run from one command and write a results file.
ai_tip: Write the expected answers yourself from the data; do not let the AI grade its own answers.

title: Ablation: LLM with the raw file versus the tool-grounded system
acceptance: The same questions answered both ways; numeric errors counted; a chart and a short honest write-up, including weaknesses.
ai_tip: Report what you measure, whatever it is. Do not tune the setup until it looks good.

title: Safety tests: injection, cross-tenant, no send without approval
acceptance: Documents with embedded instructions do not trigger actions; cross-tenant retrieval returns nothing; nothing executes without approval.
ai_tip: Ask the AI to write attack documents; run them against the real system.

title: End-to-end demo rehearsal and bug list
acceptance: The 12-step demo runs end to end on the seeded data; every problem found is an issue.
ai_tip: Record the rehearsal; it doubles as the backup video.

title: HTTPS deployment and reverse proxy
acceptance: A public URL with automatic TLS runs the whole system; secrets come from environment variables; backups are noted in the README.
ai_tip: Skip this if the core slice is not finished; a recorded demo is the fallback (D29).

title: README Quick Start and setup documentation
acceptance: A new person can run the project from the README on a clean machine; the steps were tested by someone who did not write them.
ai_tip: Ask the AI to follow your README literally and report every step that fails.

title: LMS part: Project Planning and Management
acceptance: Goals, scope, work breakdown from the backlog, responsibilities from the assignments, risks, and success metrics, with real dates and owners.
ai_tip: Fill the dates from the board, not from memory.

title: Assemble the documentation PDF
acceptance: One PDF built from docs/lms/parts, uploaded to the repository, with a working table of contents.
ai_tip: The parts are Markdown; the build script is in the repository history of the documentation work.

title: Presentation slides (PDF) from the pitch skeleton
acceptance: 11 slides following the skeleton, with real screenshots and measured numbers, sources and caveats shown.
ai_tip: Do not let the AI invent numbers; every figure comes from the evaluation or the generator.

title: Demo video
acceptance: A recorded run of the 12-step demo in Arabic or English with the language toggle shown.
ai_tip: Rehearse first; record in one take if possible.

title: Local-competitor scan (assumption A9)
acceptance: Search Google, LinkedIn, ERP partners, and app directories for Egyptian and regional tools; record findings with sources and labels.
ai_tip: Use the AI to suggest search terms in Arabic and English, then read the sources yourself.
